chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v01] Now the fitting cluster of mantras is explained in order, for the accomplishment of those not yet risen to reflection.

[tal-a30-v10] Taking from support power to trident peak, one should worship with fire, air, earth, water, sixth vowel, and bindu.

[tal-a30-v02] Indeed those awakened mantras, whose nature is reflection alone, are endowed with agency from the freedom of the free consciousness-light.

[tal-a30-v03] The mantras that enter the teacher, from established identity, make him free, and the instruments too attain agency.

[tal-a30-v04] In the support power, earth and so forth, they say the ordered four-letter set is hrim, kshlam, kshvim, vam, ksham.

[tal-a30-v05] Ham in the channel, yam, ram, lam, vam in the duty fourfold, and rim, rrim, lim, llim in the fourfold, arise in reverse order.

[tal-a30-v06] Om, aum, this threefold in knowledge, maya, and kala; anusvara and visarga belong to knowledge, lord, and supreme principle.

[tal-a30-v07] The letters from ka to bha are in the filaments; prana with eight vowels and bindu is in the eight petals; one's own name is illumined.

[tal-a30-v08] For the nine powers, sha-sha-sa with bindu are in three circles; kshmam is in preta, and jram is assigned to trident peaks.

[tal-a30-v09] In separate seat worship these mantras are remembered in order; in brief worship, the first to last seed syllable is used.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C30 atha śrītantrāloke triṃśamāhnikam atha yathocitamantrakadambakaṃ trikakulakramayogi nirūpyate / tāvadvimarśānārūḍhadhiyāṃ tātsiddhaye kramāt pratibuddhā hi te mantrā vimarśaikasvabhāvakāḥ / svatantrasyaiva ciddhāmnaḥ svātantryāt kartṛtāmayāḥ yamāviśanti cācāryaṃ taṃ tādātmyanirūḍhitaḥ / svatantrīkurvate yānti karaṇānyapi kartṛtām ādhāraśaktau hrīṃ pṛthvīprabhṛtau tu catuṣṭaye / kṣlāṃ kṣvīṃ vaṃ kṣamiti prāhuḥ kramādvarṇacatuṣṭayam haṃ nāle yaṃ tathā raṃ laṃ vaṃ dharmādicatuṣṭaye / ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḷḷṃ catuṣke ca viparītakramādbhavet oṃ auṃ hastrayamityetadvidyāmāyākalātraye / anusvāravisargau ca vidyeśeśvaratattvayoḥ kādibhāntāḥ kesareṣu prāṇo@ṣṭasvarasaṃyutaḥ / sabinduko daleṣvaṣṭasvatha svaṃ nāma dīpitam śaktīnāṃ navakasya syācchaṣasā maṇḍalatraye / sabindukāḥ kṣmaṃ prete jraṃ śūlaśṛṅgeṣu kalpayet pṛthagāsanapūjāyāṃ kramānmantrā ime smṛtāḥ / saṃkṣepapūjane tu prāgādyamantyaṃ ca bījakam ādāyādhāraśaktyādiśūlaśṛṅgāntamarcayet / agnimārutapṛthvyambusaṣaṣṭhasvarabindukam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v11] The rati crest mantra of this has a face limb with short and long vowels: fire, prana, fire-destruction, time, indra, water, wind.

[tal-a30-v12] With sixth vowel, bindu, moon, and so forth, the nine self's pervasion through bindu, nada, and so on is held in the triadic head doctrine.

[tal-a30-v13] The procedure of throwing over, overcoming, awakening and establishing consciousness is thus named: that consciousness, that attainment.

[tal-a30-v14] Such is the great pervasion, proclaimed as embodied here; transformation and its dissolution are called salutation.

[tal-a30-v15] The three-syllable mantra, joined below with six long vowels, yields the six limbs beginning with the Heart; construct its faces likewise.

[tal-a30-v16] With destruction-sound seeds blazing and bindu-adorned, with jha as the breath of withdrawal, and sa with sixth vowel and drop.

[tal-a30-v17] This is the abode of Bhairava adorned with half-moon and the rest; the matrka and malini mantras were proclaimed before.

[tal-a30-v18] Then om, the name in fourth-case ending, obeisance thus in order; among Ganesha and the rest the seed is mantra where none is declared.

[tal-a30-v19] The name's first letter illumined with a, bindu and moon is the seed of all seeds, joined with fourteen and sixty.

[tal-a30-v20] Of the triad beginning with the invoked Ghora, seeds arise in order: visarga-bearing maya, hum, and ha with visarga.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ratiśekharamantro@sya vaktrāṅgaṃ hrasvadīrghakaiḥ / agniprāṇāgnisaṃhārakālendrāmbusamīraṇāḥ saṣaṣṭhasvarabirndvadhacandrādyāḥ syurnavātmanaḥ / bindunādādikā vyāptiḥ śrīmattraiśirase mate kṣepākrānticidudbodhadīpanasthāpanānyatha / tatsaṃvittistadāpattiriti saṃjñābhiśabditā etāvatī mahāvyāptirmūrtitvenātra kīrtitā / pariṇāmastallayaśca namaskāraḥ sa ucyate eṣa tryarṇojjhito@dhastāddīrghaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ svarairyutaḥ / ṣaḍaṅgāni hṛdādīni vaktrāṇyasya ca kalpayet kṣayaravalabījaistu dīptairbinduvibhūṣitaiḥ / jhakārasaṃhṛtiprāṇāḥ saṣaṣṭhasvarabindukāḥ eṣa bhairavasadmāvaścandrārdhādivibhūṣitaḥ / mātṛkāmālinīmantrau prāgeva samudāhṛtau oṃkāro@tha caturthyantā saṃjñā natiriti kramāt / gaṇeśādiṣu mantraḥ syādbījaṃ yeṣu na coditam nāmādyakṣaramākārabinducandrādidīpitam / sarveṣāmeva bījānāṃ taccaturdaśaṣaṣṭhayuk āmantritānyaghoryāditritayasya kramoditaiḥ / bījairvisargiṇī māyā huṃ hakāro visargavān

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v21] Again three invocations of the three goddesses in order; in the second word the ka-form with e-sound is recorded here.

[tal-a30-v22] Then the two-power mantra with its final letter omitted; both fire letters joined with five vowels, the two distant ones separate.

[tal-a30-v23] The astra endowed with a joins hum, ha and the visarga-bearer; the arrow again with Tara, exceeding by two half-syllables of vasu-fire letters.

[tal-a30-v24] This is the vidya of the supreme-inferior goddess in the Trika teaching, a verse of five-six-five-veda-eye-fire-eye letters.

[tal-a30-v25] In the seven beginning with Aghora there is a remainder, each letter associated, in Siddhayogishvari-mata.

[tal-a30-v26] The arrangement of the deity circle is not stained due to multiplicity; Maya is visargini, and the mantra is paratmaka with hum and phat.

[tal-a30-v27] The jiva is the pervasion of para with many divisions, stated in Trishira-shastra by Maheshin.

[tal-a30-v28] Though different in nature and entangled in many constructions, here jiva resides in prana, or prana resides in jiva.

[tal-a30-v29] By the relation of support and supported and inseparable yoga, hamsa and amrita in the middle are divided by Kalarudra.

[tal-a30-v30] Joined to Bhuvaneshas head with two anangas, brighter than bright, arranged in six chakras, it is to be known.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-punardevītrayasyāpi kramādāmantraṇatrayam / dvitīyasminpade@kāra ekārasyeha ca smṛtaḥ tataḥ śaktidvayāmantro luptaṃ tatrāntyamakṣaram / he@gnivarṇāvubhau pañcasvarayuktau parau pṛthak akārayuktāvastraṃ huṃ ha visargī punaḥ śaraḥ / tāreṇa saha vasvagnivarṇārdhārṇadvayādhikā eṣā parāparādevyā vidyā śrītrikaśāsane / pañcaṣaṭpañcavedākṣivahninetrākṣaraṃ padam aghoryādau saptake syāt pivanyāḥ pariśiṣṭakam / pratyekavarṇago@pyuktaḥ siddhayogīśvarīmate devatācakravinyāsaḥ sa bahutvānna lipyate / māyā visargiṇī huṃ phaṭ ceti mantro@parātmakaḥ parāyāstūktasadvyāptirjīvaḥ sahacaturdaśaḥ / sānekabhedā triśiraḥśāstre proktā maheśinā svarūpato vibhinnāpi racanānekasaṅkulā / jīvaḥ prāṇastha evātra prāṇo vā jīvasaṃsthitaḥ ādhārādheyabhāvena avinābhāvayogataḥ / haṃsaṃ cāmṛtamadhyasthaṃ kālarudravibheditam bhuvaneśaśiroyuktamanaṅgadvayayojitam / dīptāddīptataraṃ jñeyaṃ ṣaṭcakrakramayojitam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v31] Prana in staff posture is united with secret shakti desire; this supreme is spoken as vacika from the nature of great knowledge.

[tal-a30-v32] This clear Bhairava heart knowledge is the one-syllable supreme nectar, alone in space, or with Savitri.

[tal-a30-v33] The supreme heart of para, endowed with two voids, well known in paired sacrifice, is to be done by knowers of tattva.

[tal-a30-v34] Other one-syllable mantras are hidden, more hidden by Ekavira rite, and devoid of limbs and family.

[tal-a30-v35] They are to be worshipped by siddha leaders, abiding in kula and giving siddhi, through kula rite with subtle knowledge yoga.

[tal-a30-v36] These are to be performed always, O goddess, by woman or man, with sa joined with six longs, limbs and faces.

[tal-a30-v37] That supreme one, joined with five short vowels and kha and accompanied by five om syllables, becomes the five-syllabled mantra, the heart of the vidya limb.

[tal-a30-v38] In amrita and tejomala, om together with svaha becomes the eleven-syllabled brahma head in the tanmalini view.

[tal-a30-v39] The crest, joined with om and so forth, with hum and phat, is for vajrin and vajradhara, preceded by svaha and om.

[tal-a30-v40] The eleven-syllabled armor, remembered as purush praised, includes tara, two-tongued, and life with kha sha ra vowels pair.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prāṇaṃ daṇḍāsanasthaṃ tu guhyaśaktīcchayā yutam / pareyaṃ vācikoddiṣṭā mahājñānasvarūpataḥ sphuṭaṃ bhairavahṛjjñānamidaṃ tvekākṣaraṃ param / amṛtaṃ kevalaṃ khasthaṃ yadvā sāvitrikāyutam śūnyadvayasamopetaṃ parāyā hṛdayaṃ param / yugmayāge prasiddhaṃ tu kartavyaṃ tattvavedibhiḥ anye@pyekākṣarā ye tu ekavīravidhānataḥ / guptā guptatarāste tu aṃgābhijanavarjitāḥ yaṣṭavyāḥ sādhakendraistu kulasthāḥ siddhidāyakāḥ / kulakramavidhānena sūkṣmavijñānayogataḥ anuṣṭheyāḥ sadā devi striyā vā puruṣeṇa vā / sakāro dīrghaṣaṭkena yukto@ṅgānyānanāni tu syāt sa eva paraṃ hrasvapañcasvarakhasaṃyutaḥ / oṃkāraiḥ pañcabhirmantro vidyāṅgahṛdayaṃ bhavet praṇavaścāmṛte tejomālini svāhayā saha / ekādaśākṣaraṃ brahmaśirastanmālinīmate vedavedani hūṃ phaṭca praṇavādiyutā śikhā / vajriṇe vajradharāya svāhetyoṃkārapūrvakam ekādaśākṣaraṃ varma puruṣṭutamiti smṛtam / tāro dvijihvaḥ khaśarasvarayugjīva eva ca

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v41] This radiant eye, common to all, is remembered; tara, shlim, beast, hum, and phat form that weapon of rasa color.

[tal-a30-v42] With long lara taksha vaya joined with bindu, indra and others have those weapons; short forms belong to vishnu and prajapati.

[tal-a30-v43] In memory, by fourth and second short forms in the lotus wheel, the classes nama, svaha, vaushat, hum, vashat, and phat arise.

[tal-a30-v44] In the six limbs in order, those classes are of that nature in rites, in recitation, offering, nourishing, agitating, and pacifying.

[tal-a30-v45] In hostile rites, for mantras, the classes from namaskara onward are second, going to eye and six sage groups with bindu.

[tal-a30-v46] By yoni syllable, the seats of mothers, with time drawing, are approved, whether omitted at beginning or end.

[tal-a30-v47] Life, standing inside the prana fold, with radiance equal to time fire, is very radiant and adorned with the left foot on the head with bindu.

[tal-a30-v48] This form following the right knee, worshipped by all mother groups, grants desired fruit to all living beings.

[tal-a30-v49] This supreme reality belongs to the mothers and to Bhairava, so the mantra practitioner who desires supreme accomplishment should recite it.

[tal-a30-v50] Rudra power entry is always established here, because this supreme power is declared as distinct from another.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-netrametatprakāśātma sarvasādhāraṇaṃ smṛtam / tāraḥ ślīṃ paśu huṃ phat ca tadastraṃ rasavarṇakam laraṭakṣavayairdīrghaiḥ samayuktaiḥ sabindukaiḥ / indrādayastadastrāṇi hrasvairviṣṇuprajāpatī smṛtau turyadvitīyābhyāṃ hrasvābhyāṃ padmacakrake / namaḥ svāhā tathā vauṣaṭ huṃ vaṣaṭ phaṭ ca jātayaḥ aṅgeṣu kramaśaḥ ṣaṭsu karmasvatha tadātmikāḥ / jape home tathāpyāye samuccāṭe@tha śāntike abhicāre ca mantrāṇāṃ namaskārādijātayaḥ / akṣiṣaṇmunivargebhyo dvitīyāḥ saha bindunā yonyarṇena ca mātṝṇāṃ sadmāvaḥ kālakarṣiṇī / ādyojjhito vāpyantena varjito vātha saṃmataḥ jīvaḥ prāṇapuṭāntaḥsthaḥ kālānalasamadyutiḥ / atidīptastu vāmāṃghrirbhūṣito mūrdhni bindunā dakṣajānugataścāyaṃ sarvamātṛgaṇārcitaḥ / anena prāṇitāḥ sarve dadate vāñchitaṃ phalam sadbhāvaḥ paramo hyeṣa mātṝṇāṃ bhairavasya ca / tasmādenaṃ japenmantrī ya icchetsiddhimuttamām rudraśaktisamāveśo nityamatra pratiṣṭhitaḥ / yasmādeṣā parā śaktirbhedenānyena kīrtitā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v51] This power performs all accomplishments found in tantra, and her limbs and faces arise by prior sound assignment.

[tal-a30-v52] Staff, living being, trident, right finger, breasts, navel, throat, wind, Rudra, and emission with trident are listed as correspondences.

[tal-a30-v53] This lord of all yogini circles is declared, and awareness arises by her utterance alone.

[tal-a30-v54] The eight-lettered form is called great fierce yoga lord, while the nine-lettered form is the more secret true being, time-drawing.

[tal-a30-v55] In the great sacrifice of Shri Damara, a beyond-beyond form is declared, with seed and cutting vowel.

[tal-a30-v56] In Malini view, the one-and-half-syllabled night of time is the knife; by repeating it one hundred times, pain arises in the head.

[tal-a30-v57] Having considered conviction, one should resort to death-conquering meditation; one desiring long life should not recite this.

[tal-a30-v58] Two staff fires, trident, sky, life, cutting, reed, peak fires with emission, and five items are placed in five locations.

[tal-a30-v59] Shiva stated in the tantra true-being teaching that the cutting knife joins the supreme.

[tal-a30-v60] One should remember this blazing weapon, joined with bindu, fire, peak, wind, and sixth vowel, from the sole of the foot to the top of the head.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yāvatyaḥ siddhayastantre tāḥ sarvāḥ kurute tviyam / aṅgavaktrāṇi cāpyasyāḥ prāgvatsvaraniyogataḥ daṇḍo jīvastriśūlaṃ ca dakṣāṅgulyaparastanau / nābhikaṇṭhau marudrudrau visargaḥ satriśūlakaḥ sarvayoginicakrāṇāmadhipo@yamudāhṛtaḥ / asyāpyuccāraṇādeva saṃvittiḥ syātpuroditā mahācaṇḍeti tu yogeśvaṛ ityaṣṭavarṇakam / navārṇeyaṃ guptatarā sadbhāvaḥ kālakarṣiṇī śrīḍāmare mahāyāge parātparataroditā / sudhācchedakaṣaṇṭhādyairbījaṃ chedakamasvaram adhyardhārṇā kālarātriḥ kṣurikā mālinīmate / śatāvartanayā hyasyā jāyate mūrdhni vedanā evaṃ pratyayamālocya mṛtyujiddhyānamāśrayet / naināṃ samuccareddevi ya iccheddīrghajīvitam dvirdaṇḍāgnī śūlanabhaḥprāṇāśchettranalau tathā / kūṭāgnī savisargāśca pañcāpyete@tha pañcasu vyomasviti śivenoktaṃ tantrasadbhāvaśāsane / chedinī kṣurikeyaṃ syādyayā yojayate pare bindvindvanalakūṭāgnimarutṣaṣṭhasvarairyutam / āpādatalamūrdhāntaṃ smaredastramidaṃ jvalat

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v61] Contract the fingers, then stimulate; crossing from knee and other chakras, contract from chakra to chakra.

[tal-a30-v62] The secret teaching giving immediate liberation is supreme; now brahma-knowledge is stated, giving immediate conviction.

[tal-a30-v63] Shiva, Sri Bhutiraja, taught us when death of all beings is imminent.

[tal-a30-v64] By which, having read and transcended, the soul goes to the stainless; even for a knower with completed duty, when heard, it is.

[tal-a30-v65] It immediately removes death-pain born from prana severance; hearing it, even one overcome by great delusion gradually attains.

[tal-a30-v66] Awakening, the speaker's presence approaches swiftly by itself; from the supreme state you have come here; eternal you, abandon the body-end.

[tal-a30-v67] From toe etc, lord, binding; indeed fierce bond; this noble statement first becomes by world-named words.

[tal-a30-v68] At ankle, knee-placed, collarbone-placed binding; likewise at groin abandon the foremost middle city; from heart-lotus you arise.

[tal-a30-v69] By these many words this noble statement is second; Hamsa, Hayagriva, lord, you are supreme Sadashiva, called Jiva.

[tal-a30-v70] Sun-moon-fire-group-drop-body, hahaha, transcend; third noble statement, by previous counts plus one words.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kuñcanaṃ cāṅgulīnāṃ tu kartavyaṃ codanaṃ tataḥ / jānvādiparacakrāntaṃ cakrāccakraṃ tu kuñcayet kathitaṃ sarahasyaṃ tu sadyonirvāṇakaṃ param / athocyate brahmavidyā sadyaḥpratyayadāyinī śivaḥ śrībhūtirājo yāmasmabhyaṃ pratyapādayat / sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ maraṇe samupasthite yayā paṭhitayotkramya jīvo yāti nirañjanam / yā jñānino@pi saṃpūrṇakṛtyasyāpi śrutā satī prāṇādicchedajāṃ mṛtyuvyathāṃ sadyo vyapohati / yāmākarṇya mahāmohavivaśo@pi kramādgataḥ prabodhaṃ vaktṛsāṃmukhyamabhyeti rabhasātsvayam / paramapadāttvamihāgāḥ sanātanastvaṃ jahīhi dehāntam pādāṅguṣṭhādi vibho nibandhanaṃ bandhanaṃ hyugram / āryāvākyamidaṃ pūrvaṃ bhuvanākhyaiḥ padairbhavet gulphānte jānugataṃ jatrusthaṃ bandhanaṃ tathā meḍhre / jahihi puramagryamadhyaṃ hṛtpadmāttvaṃ samuttiṣṭha etāvadbhiḥ padairetadāryāvākyaṃ dvitīyakam / haṃsa hayagrīva vibho sadāśivastvaṃ paro@si jīvākhyaḥ ravisomavahnisaṅghadṛbindudeho hahaha samutkrāma / tṛtīyamāryāvākyaṃ prāksaṃkhyairekādhikaiḥ padaiḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v71] Composed of the hamsa great mantra, eternal you; expecting auspicious and inauspicious; situated in the middle of the mandala; cause of the great bridge of shakti, great meaning.

[tal-a30-v72] Situated in both lotuses, come to awakening, divine body; this noble statement along with rudra-count words.

[tal-a30-v73] From ignorance you are bound; awaken and rise, O god.

[tal-a30-v74] This fifth half-verse has seven words; go to the palate-named end, the bronze-struck great gate.

[tal-a30-v75] Having reached, proceed, ho ho, or to Vamadeva station; this sixth sentence has fourteen words.

[tal-a30-v76] O lord of knots, supreme self, peaceful one, having reached the great palate hole transcend; O lord of body, quickly go to stainless Shiva station.

[tal-a30-v77] The seventh sentence may have fourteen words; the reading in the exhalation teaching says you are wind.

[tal-a30-v78] Having traversed the middle path, gathered prana and apana, and abandoned merit and demerit, Narayana, go to the peaceful end.

[tal-a30-v79] This eighth sentence has nine words: O Brahman, O Vishnu, O Rudra, you are Shiva, you are Vasudeva.

[tal-a30-v80] Destroy the eternal clay lump of Agni-Soma, O great space; this sentence is proclaimed counted by worlds.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-haṃsamahāmantramayaḥ sanātanastvaṃ śubhāśubhāpekṣī / maṇḍalamadhyaniviṣṭaḥ śaktimahāsetukāraṇamahārthaḥ kamalobhayaviniviṣṭaḥ prabodhamāyāhi devatādeha / āryāvākyamidaṃ sārdhaṃ rudrasaṃkhyapaderitam niḥśvāse tvapaśabdasya sthāne@styupa iti dhvaniḥ / ajñānāttvaṃ baddhaḥ prabodhitottiṣṭha devāde etatpañcamamāryārdhavākyaṃ syātsaptabhiḥ padaiḥ / vraja tālusāhvayāntaṃ hyauḍambaraghaṭṭitaṃ mahādvāram prāpya prayāhi haṃho haṃho vā vāmadevapadam / āryyāvākyamidaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ syāccaturdaśabhiḥ padaiḥ granthīśvara paramātman śānta mahātālurandhramāsādya / utkrama he deheśvara nirañjanaṃ śivapadaṃ prayāhyāśu āryāvākyaṃ saptamaṃ syāttaccaturdaśabhiḥ padaiḥ / prabhañjanastvamityevaṃ pāṭho niḥśvāsaśāsane ākramya madhyamārgaṃ prāṇāpānau samāhṛtya / dharmādharmau tyaktvā nārāyaṇa yāhi śāntāntam āryāvākyamidaṃ proktamaṣṭamaṃ navabhiḥ padaiḥ / he brahman he viṣṇo he rudra śivo@si vāsudevastvam agnīṣomasanātanamṛtpiṇḍaṃ jahihi he mahākāśa / etadbhuvanasaṃkhyātairāryyāvākyaṃ prakīrtitam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v81] With self, three lumps, great sheath; three words are situated in exhalation, crown, Uttara and so on.

[tal-a30-v82] Destroy the thumb-sized pure covering, O great subtle; this tenth sentence is said to have six words.

[tal-a30-v83] Enough, twice subtle; thus in Shri Mukuta Uttara, you are person bound by nature, ego thread, and bonds.

[tal-a30-v84] Renounce the supreme soul—eternally risen, of non-existence and existence—on the passionate path; this thirteen-word phrase may be the supreme noble speech.

[tal-a30-v85] O body of the hrīṃ-hūṃ mantra, come quickly without delay to the end of the body; this may be the noble half-sentence, the twelfth, six-footed, supreme.

[tal-a30-v86] Abandon this quality-made, own, six-sheathed mass; it may be the thirteenth half-āryā, with seven such words.

[tal-a30-v87] Do not take the body made of elements; take the eternal great body. This noble half-sentence, in so many words, is the fourteenth.

[tal-a30-v88] Go, having pierced this pure, endless circle situated in three ways; but this noble half-verse is fifteen by eight words.

[tal-a30-v89] This brahma knowledge with parts may have fifteen clear sentences; its five-syllable form is proclaimed without parts.

[tal-a30-v90] The reply is recited with its beginning and end joined; it comprises tāra, māyā, vedakala, mother-tāra, and the nine-formed.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sanātma tripiṇḍamiti mahākośamiti sthitam / padatrayaṃ tu niḥśvāsamukuṭottarakādiṣu aṅguṣṭhamātramamalamāvaraṇaṃ jahihi he mahāsūkṣma / āryyāvākyamidaṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ padairdaśamamucyate alaṃ dviriti sūkṣmaṃ cetyevaṃ śrīmukuṭottare / puruṣastvaṃ prakṛtimayairbaddho@haṅkāratantunā bandhaiḥ abhavābhava nityodita paramātmaṃstyaja sarāgamadhvānam / etattrayodaśapadaṃ syādāryāvākyamuttamam hrīṃhūṃmantraśarīramavilambamāśu tvamehi dehāntam / āryārdhavākyametatsyād dvādaśaṃ ṣaṭpadaṃ param tadidaṃ guṇabhūtamayaṃ tyaja sva ṣoṭkośikaṃ piṇḍam / syāt trayodaśamāryārdhaṃ padaiḥ saptabhirīdṛśam mā dehaṃ bhūtamayaṃ pragṛhyatāṃ śāśvataṃ mahādeham / āryārdhavākyaṃ tāvadbhiḥ padairetaccaturdaśam maṇḍalamamalamanantaṃ tridhā sthitaṃ gaccha bhittvaitat / āryārdhavākyamaṣṭābhiḥ padaiḥ pañcadaśaṃ tvidam sakaleyaṃ brahmavidyā syātpañcadaśabhiḥ sphuṭaiḥ / vākyaiḥ pañcākṣaraistvasyā niṣkalā parikīrtyate prativākyaṃ yayādyantayojitā paripaṭhyate / tāro māyā vedakalo mātṛtāro navātmakaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v100] Now for those without wealth and for devotees truly, the fault of place, time, and so on is not so for those with such resolve.

[tal-a30-v91] Thus, according to proclaimed pervasion, there are five syllables: bindu, prana, nectar, water, and wind endowed with the sixth vowel.

[tal-a30-v92] By this, through the seed situated in the utterance of shakti, the bound soul who has performed the initiation rite is obtained; even one who was formerly a slayer of a brahmin becomes purified.

[tal-a30-v93] By lightness the balance becomes pure and immediately causes certainty; tara, shamara, lump, and bow are four-lettered.

[tal-a30-v94] Subduing Shakini is the vital point of heart and life; but this is by sixth prana, trikuta, upraised arm, spear-named bindus.

[tal-a30-v95] The heart adorned with anacka, nose, lower face, and moon pieces is called Bhairava and is all-destroying.

[tal-a30-v96] Shakinis heated by Bhairava fire in the middle of the fire circle come under control; if this place burns.

[tal-a30-v97] Dismiss them first, otherwise they pierce; with these letters hreem, kleem, vlem, klem adorned with twelve vowels.

[tal-a30-v98] The heart named union of loved ones is a joined pair; chant it individually, or with two, or with all; this is the best rule.

[tal-a30-v99] The balance-union yoga in the Shri Tantra true-being teaching, spoken by Shambhunatha, has been shown by me in order.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-iti pañcākṣarāṇi syuḥ proktavyāptyanusārataḥ / binduprāṇāmṛtajalaṃ marutṣaṣṭhasvarānvitam etena śaktyuccārasthabījenālabhyate paśuḥ / kṛtadīkṣāvidhiḥ pūrvaṃ brahmaghno@pi viśuddhyati laghutvena tulāśuddhiḥ sadyaḥpratyayakāriṇī / tāraḥ śamarayaiḥ piṇḍo natiśca caturarṇakam śākinīstobhanaṃ marma hṛdayaṃ jīvitaṃ tvidam / ṣaṣṭhaprāṇatrikūṭordhvabāhuśūlākhyabindubhiḥ anackanāsādhovaktracandrakhaṇḍaiśca maṇḍitam / hṛdayaṃ bhairavākhyaṃ tu sarvasaṃhārakārakam agnimaṇḍalamadhyasthabhairavānalatāpitāḥ / vaśamāyānti śākinyaḥ sthānametena ceddahet visarjayettāḥ prathamamanyathā cchidrayanti tāḥ / hrīṃ klīṃ vleṃ kleṃ ebhirvarṇairdvādaśasvarabhūṣitaiḥ priyamelāpanaṃ nāma hṛdayaṃ sampuṭaṃ japet / pratyekamathavā dvābhyāṃ sarvairvā vidhiruttamaḥ tulāmelakayogaḥ śrītantrasadbhāvaśāsane / ya uktaḥ śambhunāthena sa mayā darśitaḥ kramāt atha vittavihīnānāṃ prapannānāṃ ca tattvataḥ / deśakālādidoṣeṇa na tathādhyavasāyinām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v101] Initiation should be done as told, delighted by the Shri lineage, urged by the Hatakesha Patala lord.

[tal-a30-v102] O Shri Natha, noble lord, this triad indeed: root, support, Varuna, my desire, lordship; this triad is in the heart.

[tal-a30-v103] The four named groups from dharma are in the throat region, worshipful, beginning with hreem shreem, all endowed with address and ending with foot words.

[tal-a30-v104] At the head base three knowledges are stated; then meditate by mind union, with flowers or joys, or by meditation alone.

[tal-a30-v105] When the truth-knowing guru finds a disciple heart-made for liberation alone, skilled in liberation's sole gift, this is the supreme-upanisad initiation.

[tal-a30-v106] Initiated into this initiation, remembering this threefold vidya in the heart, without outer worship and the rest, he reaches the supreme abode at body's end.

[tal-a30-v107] Om and maya with bindu: make three letters from the start into five addressed words ending with the fire-god's beloved.

[tal-a30-v108] The accomplished-accomplishing power in sound-brahman form, joined with the word of every bond, cuts.

[tal-a30-v109] In awakening, invoked by the mother of Siva's true being, the five-footed verse runs in five-eight and three-eight order.

[tal-a30-v110] The sky-five-syllable supreme-brahman vidya gives liberation, auspicious, in supreme desire with bell and thirteen tones.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prakartavyā yathā dīKṣā śrīsantatyāgamoditā / kathyate hāṭakeśānapātālādhipacoditā śrīnātha ārya bhagavannetattritayaṃ hi kanda ādhāre / varuṇo macchando bhagavatta iti trayamidaṃ hṛdaye dharmādivargasaṃjñāścatvāraḥ kaṇṭhadeśagāḥ pūjyāḥ / hrīṃśrīṃpūrvāḥ sarve sambodhajuṣaśca pādaśabdāntāḥ mūrdhatale vidyātrayamuktaṃ bhāvyatha mano@bhiyogena / kusumairānandairvā bhāvanayā vāpi kevalayā guruṇā tattvavidā kila śiṣyo yadi mokṣamātrakṛtahṛdayaḥ / mokṣaikadānacaturā dīkṣā seyaṃ paropaniṣaduktā etaddīkṣādīkṣita etadvidyātrayaṃ smaran hṛdaye / bāhyārcādi vinaiva hi vrajati paraṃ dhāma dehānte praṇavo māyā bindurvarṇatrayamāditaḥ kuryāt / padapañcakasya saṃbodhanayuktasyāgnidayitānte siddhasādhani tatpūrvaṃ śabdabrahmasvarūpiṇi / samastabandhaśabdena sahitaṃ ca nikṛntani bodhani śivasadbhāvajananyāmantritaṃ ca tat / pañcāṣṭarandhratryaṣṭārṇakrameṇa padapañcakam khapañcārṇā parabrahmavidyeyaṃ mokṣadā śivā / anuttarecche ghāntaśca satrayodaśasusvaraḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v111] At the three letters' end the four semivowels ending in ta; first-of-class and horse with triangle-bindu joined, from three letters after pa.

[tal-a30-v112] The great-golden-sound seven-syllable mantra of the goddess, addressed forgive-thus in three syllables, ending sin.

[tal-a30-v113] The six-syllabled deluding word beginning with the sinful word; then kill, shake off, in twice-twice-ten syllables, such is the word.

[tal-a30-v114] By Rudra-Sakti power the six-letter form ending in fifth case; then the one syllable declared, the visarga-brahman.

[tal-a30-v115] In union with that act recite: hole-ocean letters, this vidya called initiation-knowledge.

[tal-a30-v116] Maya-syllable in supreme brahman with four vidyas, three feet; eight syllables then five, named yoga-bearer.

[tal-a30-v117] A ten-syllabled form ending in e, situated in knowledge and made of three words, is proclaimed as the form of self, inner self, and supreme self.

[tal-a30-v118] May it be, O beloved of Rudra, that this veda-syllable Rudra-shakti burns my sin; this formula is twelve-syllabled and four-footed.

[tal-a30-v119] O gentle Sadashiva, this convention-removing formula contains a pair and six, brings bindu and arrow, and has four half-syllables.

[tal-a30-v120] This knowledge, counted as half-syllable, kha, and arrow, is the supreme lady; glorious Bhutiraja described this triad of knowledges.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-asya varṇatrayasyānte tvantaḥsthānāṃ catuṣṭayam / vargādyaśvau tryasrabinduyuk pānto@rṇatrayādataḥ mahāhāṭakaśabdādyamīśvarītyarṇasaptakam / āmantritaṃ kṣamasveti tryarṇaṃ pāpāntakāriṇi ṣaḍarṇaṃ pāpaśabdādivimohanipadaṃ tataḥ / pāpaṃ hana dhuna dvirdvirdaśārṇaṃ padamīdṛśam pañcamyantaṃ ṣaḍarṇaṃ syādrudraśaktivaśāditi / tata ekākṣaraṃ yattadvisargabrahma kīrtitam tadanackatakāreṇa sahaikībhāvataḥ paṭhet / randhrābdhivarṇā vidyeyaṃ dīkṣāvidyeti kīrtitā māyārṇañca pare brahme caturvidye padatrayam / aṣṭārṇamatha pañcārṇaṃ yogadhāriṇisaṃjñitam ātmāntarātmaparamātmarūpaṃ ca padatrayam / ekārāntaṃ bodhanasthaṃ daśārṇaṃ parikīrtitam rudraśaktīti vedārṇaṃ syādrudradayite@tha me / pāpaṃ dahadahetyeṣā dvādaśārṇā catuṣpadī saumye sadāśive yugmaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ bindviṣusāvahā / sārdhavarṇacatuṣkaṃ tadityeṣā samayāpahā vidyā sārdhārṇakhaśarasaṃkhyā sā pārameśvarī / etadvidyātrayaṃ śrīmadbhūtirājo nyarūpayat

chunks.l2:
[tal-a30-v121] The glorious Śrīkaṇṭha, who directly worshipped the human body, has power previously stated; the guru should follow it everywhere.

[tal-a30-v122] According to meaning, seed, entry, and so on, nothing at all exists that was not previously explained.

[tal-a30-v123] Repetition is fruitless to us; thus the nature of mantra knowledge and so on has been described.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yaḥ sākṣādabhajacchrīmāñśrīkaṇṭho mānuṣīṃ tanum / atra vīryaṃ puraivoktaṃ sarvatrānusaredguruḥ arthabījapraveśāntaruccārādyanusārataḥ / nahi tatkiṃcanāpyasti yatpurā na nirūpitam niṣphalā punaruktistu nāsmabhyaṃ jātu rocate / ityevaṃ mantravidyādisvarūpamupavarṇitam
